## Three ways to combine models {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Chained**

Run one model on the output of the last. Prevalence feeds incidence and
$R_t$, and those feed transmissibility and severity.

Flexible, quick, and the uncertainty is approximated at each step while
assumptions are inherited unchecked, which biases what comes out.
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Joint**

Fit every data source in one model. England's COVID-19 models fitted
cases, prevalence, severity and bed occupancy together, and that
evidence reached policy.

Rigorous, and it hands you a model nobody can take apart. When mpox
spread through sexual contact networks in 2022, those models were not
adapted to it, and new single-source ones were built at speed.
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Composable**

Validate each part on its own, then compose the parts and fit
everything together.

Components carry their own priors, so domain knowledge travels with the
component rather than with the person. Model definitions do not know
about the data, so one definition simulates and fits.
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
The trade-off is not between good and bad models. It is between rigour
and being able to move.
:::

::: {.attribution}
Birrell et al. (2025),
[doi:10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf030](https://doi.org/10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf030) ·

## EpiNow2, rebuilt out of parts {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- An ARIMA(2,1,1) latent process and a negative binomial observation
  model, both lifted unchanged from other applications
- `broadcast_weekly` for weekly $R_t$, day-of-week ascertainment around
  the observation model, and two `LatentDelay` wrappers for the
  incubation period and the reporting delay
- **A** to **D** validate each part on its own. **E** and **F** are the
  joint fit, recovering cases through the delays and $R_t$ with them

::: {.callout-important}
Nothing here required editing a component that already existed. The
parts were validated separately and the composition was fitted
together. That is the whole claim.
:::

::: {.attribution}
One of three replications in the paper, alongside a renewal model of
South Korea and an ODE model of influenza. Replicating
[EpiNow2](https://doi.org/10.12688/wellcomeopenres.16006.2)
(Abbott et al., 2020). Figures from the paper,
[doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675)
:::
